2608.26846.title: Evaluating Confidence-Gated Retrieval with Matched Trajectory Replay
2608.26846.paper_summary: Interactive language-model agents use confidence signals to decide whether to answer immediately, retrieve additional evidence (from memory or external knowledge), or defer. Yet confidence is usually evaluated in isolation, without measuring the trajectory-level consequences of the actions it triggers. We propose matched trajectory replay, a controlled protocol for comparing confidence-to-action mappings. The protocol holds candidate answer states, evidence points, budgets, and action costs fixed. We use it to compare raw verbalized confidence with post-hoc isotonic calibration in a multi-hop question-answering system using Mistral, GPT, and Qwen models on HotpotQA and MuSiQue datasets. At the same numerical commitment threshold, calibration changes which questions agents ultimately commit to answering. Across all six model-dataset pairs, it increases accuracy among committed answers by up to 41 percentage points. However, it can reduce coverage and increase retrieval use. Overall accuracy improves by up to 15 percentage points on HotpotQA but falls by up to 17 percentage points on MuSiQue. These effects reflect a shift to a more selective, lower-risk operating point, not improved answers or confidence ranking. A calibration map fitted before retrieval improves held-out calibration through retrieval depths one and two, but is worse than raw confidence at depth three for all three models. Additional evidence helps on average, but this aggregate effect does not establish whether confidence identifies which individual episodes will benefit from another retrieval. Taken together, these results show that calibration can make commitment risk interpretable, but it does not estimate the expected benefit of another retrieval. Retrieval therefore requires a separate value-of-information or utility estimate. Evaluations should report held-out calibration, risk-coverage, and retrieval cost.
2608.26846.paper_summary_zh: 互動語言模型代理使用信心信號來決定是否立即回答、檢索額外證據（來自記憶或外部知識）或延遲。然而，信心通常是孤立評估的，沒有衡量其觸發的行動的軌跡級後果。我們提出了匹配軌跡重播，這是一種比較信心與行動映射的受控協議。該協議保持候選答案狀態、證據點、預算和行動成本不變。我們用它來比較在使用 Mistral、GPT 和 Qwen 模型的多跳問答系統中，原始口頭表達的信心與事後等級校準在 HotpotQA 和 MuSiQue 數據集上的表現。在相同的數值承諾閾值下，校準改變了代理最終承諾回答的問題。在所有六個模型-數據集對中，它使承諾答案的準確性提高了最多 41 個百分點。然而，它可能會降低覆蓋率並增加檢索使用。在 HotpotQA 上，整體準確性提高了最多 15 個百分點，但在 MuSiQue 上下降了最多 17 個百分點。這些效果反映了轉向更具選擇性、風險較低的操作點，而不是改進答案或信心排名。在檢索之前擬合的校準圖在檢索深度一和二時改善了保持的校準，但在深度三時對所有三個模型來說，表現不如原始信心。額外證據平均上是有幫助的，但這種整體效果並未確定信心是否能識別哪些個別事件將從另一個檢索中受益。綜合來看，這些結果顯示校準可以使承諾風險可解釋，但它並不估計另一個檢索的預期收益。因此，檢索需要單獨的信息價值或效用估計。評估應報告保持的校準、風險覆蓋和檢索成本。
